evidence_quotes.quote: This policy review informs on wastewater discharge (and related) standards for sewage treatment plants within the context of present-day India.

In this paper, the outputs of a broader evidence review based on Indian policies and regulations and complementary interviews with governmental institutions, sectoral experts, and technology providers in India are combined to analyze and understand pollution control measures and approaches that focus on municipal domestic sewage treatment and wastewater reuse.
All historically applicable wastewater discharge standards for STPs in India were considered for the assessment.
Interviewees have requested strict anonymity and that no data from qualitative interviews to be presented that can be traced to individuals and institutions. Hence only insights have been presented.

evidence_quotes.quote: By comparison, the implementation of just one set of standards for both discharge to inland water and use on land in India is regressive with international practice and discourages nutrient recycling.

criterion_notes.c1: Does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access. The paper focuses on environmental pollution control regulations—specifically effluent discharge standards for municipal sewage treatment plants (STPs) and water quality standards for treated wastewater reuse (such as agricultural irrigation and urban/industrial non-potable reuse).
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 (yes under plain wording) because it examines statutory, regulatory, and judicial instruments governing wastewater management in India (including the Water Act 1974, Environment Protection Act 1986, MoEF&CC STP discharge notifications, CPCB norms, National Green Tribunal orders, Karnataka's Urban Wastewater Reuse Policy, and international frameworks). However, it fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading (no under active reading) because these regulations set chemical and microbiological effluent discharge and reuse limits for STPs to control river pollution and guide resource recovery, rather than rule-type mechanisms directly governing household or community water or sanitation service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, tenure/documentation rules, consumer tariffs, or disconnection). Even under the plain reading of Criterion 2, the overall decision remains exclude because Criteria 1, 4, and 5 are not met.
criterion_notes.c3: Published as a Policy and Practice Review combining a review of governmental regulations and secondary CPCB reports with anonymous qualitative interviews of governmental officials, sectoral experts, and technology providers; however, no sample size, interview protocol, or systematic qualitative coding method is reported, and the Author's Note states that no primary data from the qualitative interviews are presented.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports regulatory effluent parameter thresholds (BOD, COD, TSS, pH, nutrients, fecal coliforms), secondary STP technology removal performance and capital cost per MLD, and narrative discussion of STP retrofitting and compliance challenges; reports no empirical outcome measuring household or community service access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: No household or community population, service-access outcome, or empirical sample size is reported; the unit of discussion is national/state STP effluent regulation and anonymous informant perspectives without presented primary data.

study_design: Policy and practice review (regulatory document review supplemented by unattributed qualitative informant insights)
country: India (with international regulatory comparisons including the European Union, Ireland, France, Tanzania, Ecuador, and Jordan)
population_and_sample: National and state STP effluent regulatory frameworks in India (plus international regulatory comparators); anonymous governmental officials, sectoral experts, and technology providers interviewed (sample size not reported)
exposure: Wastewater effluent discharge standards and treated wastewater reuse regulations for sewage treatment plants (MoEF&CC notifications, CPCB guidelines, and National Green Tribunal orders)
outcome: Permissible STP effluent and reuse water quality parameters (BOD, COD, TSS, nutrients, pH, fecal coliforms), secondary STP technology cost/performance comparisons, and narrative stakeholder perspectives on regulatory feasibility (no household or community service access outcome reported)
rationale: Excluded (E01 - Wrong topic). This Policy and Practice Review examines environmental pollution control regulations—specifically effluent discharge limits for municipal sewage treatment plants (STPs) and water quality standards for treated wastewater reuse (primarily agricultural irrigation)—in India alongside international comparisons. It does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access (c1 = no), does not examine a rule-type legal/administrative mechanism governing household or community service access under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 scope (c2 = no; though it discusses environmental regulatory standards under plain wording, plain_criterion2_decision is still exclude due to failing c1, c4, and c5), presents only narrative policy review and unattributed informant insights with interview data withheld (c3 = unclear), and reports no empirical service-access outcome (c4 = no).
